prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objective “best” lawyer for every truck accident — the right attorney depends on your case details (severity of injuries, whether the trucker or carrier is commercial, any fatalities, whether a government driver is involved, etc.) and what you need (trial experience vs. a firm that negotiates big settlements).

A few quick questions so I can point you to the attorneys most likely to fit your case:
- Are you the injured person, a family member, or a representative of someone else?
- Where in Dallas did the crash occur, and when did it happen?
- Are there serious / catastrophic injuries or a death?
- Do you already have an attorney?
- Do you need someone who speaks a language other than English?

If you’d like recommendations, I can compile a short vetted list for you. To help now, here’s how to identify a strong truck-accident lawyer and what to ask at a free consult.

What to look for
- Substantial truck-accident experience (not just general PI). Trucking cases involve FMCSA rules, logbooks, black boxes, company safety records, cargo/load rules, and multi-party litigation.
- Trial experience and a record of large verdicts/settlements in truck cases.
- Resources to hire accident reconstructionists, medical experts, and investigators.
- Familiarity with federal and state trucking regulations (FMCSA) and how to subpoena driver logs and ELD/black-box data.
- Clear contingency-fee agreement (you pay only if they recover).
- Good client communication and local Dallas/Collin/Denton County courtroom presence.
- Board certification in civil trial law (optional but valuable).
- Positive reviews, peer ratings (Martindale-Hubbell), and no serious disciplinary history.

Questions to ask at the consultation
- How many truck cases have you handled? How many went to trial?
- Have you handled cases against X (the specific carrier/insurer if known)?
- What results have you obtained for truck accident clients?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day? (Partner vs. associate)
- What experts would you retain and when?
- How do you charge? What percentage and what costs would be deducted?
- How long do you expect my case to take?
- Can you provide client references?

Red flags
- Guarantees of a specific dollar amount.
- Reluctance to go to trial or no trial experience.
- Pressure to sign immediately or unclear fee terms.
- Poor communication or vague answers about who handles the case.

Deadline note
- In Texas the usual personal injury statute of limitations is 2 years from the accident date (wrongful death is 2 years from death). Claims against government entities may have much shorter notice requirements. If your case is recent, act quickly.

If you want, I can:
- Provide a short list (3–6) of well-regarded Dallas truck-accident attorneys/firms based on known reputations up to mid‑2024;
- Or help draft an email/message you can send to law firms to screen them.

Which would you prefer?
